$comment: Riftlight, Wandering Sky strand end (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, squall-temple; design note squall-temple-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 to the Borrowed Ruins pilot's bar. Question: can we keep the temple safe as the island drifts in? Keeper Clove, the temple's kitsune keeper, carries it with Pip Thistledown. Bone crawlers from the far-off coast show the pull reaches everywhere. Reads island_warning_sent / island_relay_delayed / island_messages_saved; sets temple_island_settled (the island let settle) and temple_damaged (the landing fight lost).
title: The Temple in the Squall

plate.narration: Rain sweeps across a temple island high above the realm. Wind banners stream over the wet landing. Through the clouds, another island appears for a moment, then fades behind the rain.

goal.text: Can we keep the temple safe as the island drifts in?

steps.label: Bring Pip back from the island
Meet the island at the landing

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The storm is loud, not cruel; the crawlers are homesick, not wicked; nobody dies.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Keeper Clove: Keeper Clove, the Squall Temple's kitsune keeper (he/him). Fussy, kind and brave when it counts; glasses always fogged, teapot always in hand, keeps a weather book. Has never met an island. Wants the bell rung and every keeper dry.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants to impress her. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.
npcVoices.Tumble: Tumble, a young griffin island courier (she/her). Fast, cheerful and terrible at landing; carries letters and messages between the islands.

arrival.narration: A cloud skiff from Juniper's lookout bucks toward a temple island in the rain, all red roofs and ringing bells. Pip Thistledown clings to the mast. On the landing, a kitsune in a brown apron waves a teapot like a lantern. "Keeper Clove, of the Squall Temple!" he shouts. "Notchbrow is drifting straight at us, with a storm behind it. Can we keep the temple safe as the island drifts in? Jump, quick!"

variants.text: "Your warning came in time. My keepers are safe inside!"
"Your warning only just got here. Half my keepers are still outside!"
"We heard the welcome song! My keepers are all out on the landing with lanterns, to greet it!"

check_skiff.narration: The skiff rises and falls beside the landing like a rocking horse. The gap opens and closes.
check_skiff.prompt: Jump from the bucking skiff onto the wet landing

onSuccess.narration: You land neatly. Pip lands on you. The skiff bobs away home.

onFailure.narration: You land in a rain barrel. Splash! Clove fishes you out by the collar, and your snacks float away. "Welcome," he says. "You are wet."

tear.narration: Something is wrong by the bell tower. A tear in the air flickers at its door, and little pale creatures clatter out of it, in shells made of old bone chips. Bone crawlers! They live far away on the coast, in a mudflat full of giant old bones. Clove has never seen one. "What are they doing in the sky?" They swarm toward the bells' hum, and toward your humming chime. The chime leans hard toward the glacier. Whatever is pulling Notchbrow is pulling these too.

variants.text: Up on the temple roof, Tumble the courier waves a wing. "Flew ahead!" she calls. "Landed on a goose."

first.narration: Clove wrings his paws. "The weather bell must ring before the squall hits, so every island ties down its washing and its little ones. But the crawlers are climbing the tower to nibble its hum!" Down on the landing, the littlest keeper, a kitsune called Fig, has climbed the tallest lantern post to watch for the island. The rain is getting heavier. What first?

variants.text: "Everyone else is inside, thanks to your warning. Fig sneaked out."
"And half my keepers are still out there with her!"
"And all my keepers are out there with her, holding welcome lanterns!"

tower_stairs.narration: The tower stairs are wet and steep, and they go around and around. Crawlers clatter somewhere above. Pip counts the steps out loud and loses count at nine.
tower_stairs.prompt: Race up the slippery tower stairs before the crawlers reach the bell

onSuccess.narration: You burst out at the top just as the first crawler does.

onFailure.narration: You slip and bang a knee. At the top, a crawler is already nibbling the bell rope.

fight_bell.narration: Ring the weather bell by ending two turns beside it, or drive the crawlers off the tower.

bell_rung.narration: Bong! The weather bell rolls out across the sky. Far away, another island's bell answers, and another, and another, until the whole sky is ringing. Everywhere, keepers are tying down their washing. Clove wipes his foggy glasses. "Every island heard that," he says.

variants.text: The clang sends the crawlers tumbling down the tower, holding their heads.
You chase the last crawler off the tower, and they scatter across the wet roofs. Then you ring the bell yourselves.
Down on the landing, Fig hears it and climbs down by herself.

clapper_gone.narration: The crawlers pile on and push you back down the stairs. When you climb up again, the bell is still there, but its clapper is gone. Three crawlers are carrying it off across the roof like a prize. Pip bangs the bell with his spoon. Tink. "Well," he says. "I heard it." No other island will.

variants.text: Down on the landing, Fig gives up waiting and climbs down by herself.

keepers_soaked.narration: Down on the landing, the squall got there first. The keepers stagger in, soaked to the fur, their lanterns blown out. Clove climbs the lantern post himself to fetch Fig down, and he loses his teapot on the way. Fig sneezes. "Never mind," Clove says bravely. "Teapots can be found. Bells can't be late."

variants.text: Down on the landing, there is nobody to fetch. Your warning got everyone inside, and Fig came down by herself. Clove pats your arm. "You thought of everything," he says.

landing.narration: Out on the landing, the rain comes sideways. Fig clings to the top of the swaying lantern post, and she won't let go. "Fig!" Clove calls. "Down, please!" Behind you, up on the tower, the crawlers are nibbling the bell rope.

choices.label: Make a chain and lead everyone in
Ask Tumble to lift Fig down
Call Fig down, kitsune to kitsune
Brace the hall door against the wind

variants.text: Everyone else is safe inside. It's just Fig.
Half the keepers huddle under the stairs, soaked.
All the other keepers are out here too, holding welcome lanterns that keep blowing out.

check_chain.narration: Everyone grabs a paw, a hand or a tail. The wind tugs at the chain like a kite string.
check_chain.prompt: Hold the chain together in the wind and lead everyone in

onSuccess.narration: Step by step, the chain reaches the hall door. Fig climbs down at last and joins the end.

onFailure.narration: A gust knocks the chain over like dominoes. Everyone gets in, soaked and bruised, and a lantern blows away into the clouds.

check_climb.narration: The lantern post is slick with rain and sways in the gusts. Fig peeks down at you with huge eyes.
check_climb.prompt: Climb the swaying post and carry Fig down

onSuccess.narration: You reach Fig, and she wraps around your neck like a scarf. Down you come. Clove herds the others inside.

onFailure.narration: You slide down the post with Fig on your head. Bump. Bruised, but down. Clove herds everyone inside.

tumble_lift.narration: Tumble swoops low, scoops Fig off the post and drops her, very gently, into Clove's arms. Then Tumble lands in a rain barrel. "Meant to," she says, from inside it. Everyone hurries in.

foxfire.narration: You flick your tail the kitsune way, low and slow. Fig flicks hers back and slides down the post like a raindrop. The others follow you in, giggling.

brace.narration: Your thornguard braces the hall door with a skill called Brace, so the wind can't slam it. Clove plucks Fig off the post, and everyone runs in through the steady door. Nobody gets blown anywhere.

keepers_in.narration: The last keeper is in. Clove counts tails, wings and dripping hats, twice. Then, up on the tower, the bell rope snaps. The crawlers have chewed it through, and the weather bell falls silent. Clove looks up at it. "The other islands won't hear our warning tonight," he says quietly. "But my keepers are dry."

choices.label: Climb up and knot the rope

check_knot.narration: The tower stairs are slick, and the crawlers are still up there, nibbling. The two ends of the bell rope dangle out of reach.
check_knot.prompt: Climb past the crawlers and knot the bell rope back together

onSuccess.narration: You knot the rope and give it one big pull. Bong! The crawlers tumble off the tower, holding their heads. It's late, but far away the other islands' bells answer.

onFailure.narration: A crawler nips your fingers and the knot slips loose. You slide back down the stairs. The bell stays silent.

stay_together.narration: You stay. Fig climbs into Clove's apron pocket, which is a very big pocket. Clove pats it. "A bell is a bell," he says. "These are my keepers." Up on the tower, the crawlers click and nibble the silent bell.

hall.narration: Inside, the hall smells of wet fur and ginger. Clove hands out towels as big as flags. Through the round window, Notchbrow is a dark shape in the rain, coming closer. Pip wrings out his tail into a teacup, by accident.

pip_gone.narration: Then Clove looks around. "Where's your manticore?" Pip's teacup is empty, and a long push pole is missing from the rack. Out in the rain, Notchbrow has drifted close to the landing. A small figure stands on its edge, shoving at it with the pole. "Lady Olivia says one good shove!" Pip yells. The island does not notice.

choices.label: Push a plank across and crawl
Ask Tumble to fly you over

check_jump.narration: The gap between the landing and Notchbrow opens and closes like a yawn.
check_jump.prompt: Jump the yawning gap onto the island's edge

onSuccess.narration: You land in soft wet grass, right beside Pip's footprints.

onFailure.narration: You land short and scramble up the grass on your elbows, muddy to the ears.

check_plank.narration: The plank is long and heavy, and the gap keeps changing its mind.
check_plank.prompt: Shove the long plank across the gap and hold it while everyone crawls over

onSuccess.narration: The plank lands on the grass, and you crawl across one by one.

onFailure.narration: The plank slips and slaps the grass. You crawl over the wobbly end, and somebody gets a splinter the size of a pencil.

tumble_fly.narration: Tumble flaps you over the gap a few at a time, and lands, for once, perfectly. "Did you see that?" she shouts. "Somebody tell Juniper!"

fly_pip.narration: Your griffin swoops over the gap and back, over and back, until everyone is across. The rain doesn't even have time to aim.

on_notchbrow.narration: Notchbrow again! The crooked orchard, the old scarecrow, and the hen, sitting in Pip's dropped hat as if it were a nest. She glares at you. You have met before. Pip is beside the old mooring stone, shoving his pole against the ground with all his might.

pip_found.narration: Notchbrow does not move one inch. Rain drips off Pip's ears. "Lady Olivia would push it," he puffs. "I wanted to show her I could do it by myself." Beside him, the mooring stone hums along with your chime. What do you do?

choices.label: Sit with him and watch where it's going

pip_shove.narration: Everyone grabs the pole. Pip counts to three, and then to three again, louder. You heave. The pole bends like a noodle, and everyone sits down hard in the wet grass. Notchbrow does not notice at all. Pip stares at the pole. "Oh," he says. "An island is bigger than a shove." Then he laughs until he hiccups.

pip_watch.narration: You sit beside Pip in the rain. Notchbrow creaks toward the glacier, and your chime leans with it. Pip watches for a long time. "It isn't wandering," he says slowly. "It's being pulled. Pushing can't fix being pulled." He lays the pole down in the grass.

check_hop.narration: Notchbrow's edge swings toward the landing and away. The gap is a hop, then a leap, then a hop again.
check_hop.prompt: Hop back to the landing with Pip before the gap opens wide

onSuccess.narration: You hop back with Pip between you. Clove catches him by the scarf.

onFailure.narration: You jump on a leap instead of a hop. You make it, just, and land in a heap with Pip on top.

towels.narration: Clove throws towels over everyone. "Never do that again," he tells Pip, "or I'll tie a bell to your tail." Pip peeks out from under his towel. "Sorry," he mumbles. "I just wanted Lady Olivia to say I did something big." What do you tell him?

choices.label: That was brave, and a bit silly

pip_brave.narration: Pip grins under his towel. "Brave and silly," he repeats. "Lady Olivia says those go together." He writes it on his paw so he won't forget, and the ink runs down his wrist.

pip_asks.narration: Pip thinks about it. Then he holds out his paw to shake on it, very seriously, like a grown-up. "Next time I'll tell you first," he says. "Then we can all be silly together."

weather_book.narration: By the fire, Clove opens a huge book of weather and islands. "Every year we write down who drifts past," he says. "This year, three islands came early, all leaning the same way. And now crawlers, from a field of old bones on the coast, so far away I've never seen it." He taps the page. Your chime leans the same way, toward the glacier. Whatever is pulling Notchbrow reaches everywhere.

rest.narration: Clove's keepers bring rice buns, hot and sticky. Through the window, Notchbrow fills the sky. "Now we choose," says Clove. "Push it clear with the long poles, and the temple is safe, but Notchbrow drifts on into the storm, still pulled. Or clear the landing and let it settle against us. It can rest at last, but it will bring the crawlers right to our door and squash my landing rail."

variants.text: "Let it settle," says Pip quietly. "It's tired."
"Push it," says Pip. "All together this time."

push_plan.narration: You'll push. Clove's keepers fetch the long push poles from the rack. "A small turn," Clove says. "Not a shove across the sky." Pip spits on his paws, then wipes them on Clove's apron.

choices.label: Haul the poles out to the landing
Use the poles your warning got ready

variants.text: Out on the landing, your warning's poles are already braced and waiting.

check_poles.narration: The push poles are long, heavy and as slippery as eels.
check_poles.prompt: Haul the heavy push poles out and brace them on the landing

onSuccess.narration: The poles are braced against the posts, ready.

onFailure.narration: A pole slips and lands on a foot. Ouch. But the poles are braced, ready.

shelter_plan.narration: You'll let it settle. Clove's keepers drag out every cushion in the temple to pad the landing. "Gently," Clove tells the island, as if it can hear. Pip carries a cushion bigger than he is.

choices.label: Use the landing your welcome cleared

variants.text: Out on the landing, the keepers who came to greet the island have already swept it clear and lined it with cushions.

check_cushions.narration: The rain soaks the cushions almost as fast as you can carry them.
check_cushions.prompt: Stack the cushions into a soft wall before they get soggy

onSuccess.narration: A fat, soft wall of cushions lines the landing.

onFailure.narration: Half the cushions are soggy and flat by the time you stack them. It will have to do.

approach_push.narration: Notchbrow's edge looms out of the rain, right at the landing. Out of the tear by the tower pour the bone crawlers, rushing toward the island's fresh magic and your humming chime. "Poles!" shouts Clove.

choices.label: To the poles, while the crawlers are dizzy

variants.text: The weather bell's ring still hums in the air, and some of the crawlers wobble, dizzy.
With no bell ringing, nothing slows them down. There are a lot of crawlers.

approach_shelter.narration: Notchbrow's edge looms out of the rain, right at the landing. Out of the tear by the tower pour the bone crawlers, rushing toward the island's fresh magic and your humming chime. "Hold the landing!" shouts Clove.

choices.label: Hold it while the crawlers are dizzy

variants.text: The weather bell's ring still hums in the air, and some of the crawlers wobble, dizzy.
With no bell ringing, nothing slows them down. There are a lot of crawlers.

fight_push.narration: Swing Notchbrow clear by ending three turns beside the push poles, or drive the crawlers off. Gusts knock everyone about, and the crosswind shoves anyone who stops in it. The bell has some of the crawlers dizzy.

fight_push_swarm.narration: Swing Notchbrow clear by ending three turns beside the push poles, or drive the crawlers off. Gusts knock everyone about, and the crosswind shoves anyone who stops in it. With no bell ringing, the whole swarm comes.

fight_shelter.narration: Hold the cushioned landing for two rounds while Notchbrow settles, or drive the crawlers off. Gusts knock everyone about, and the crosswind shoves anyone who stops in it. The bell has the crawlers dizzy, so it settles quickly.

fight_shelter_swarm.narration: Hold the cushioned landing for three rounds while Notchbrow settles, or drive the crawlers off. Gusts knock everyone about, and the crosswind shoves anyone who stops in it. With no bell ringing, the crawlers keep coming, so it takes longer.

pushed.narration: The poles bite. Slowly, slowly, Notchbrow's edge turns past the landing, and the island drifts away into the rain, still leaning toward the glacier. The temple is safe. Clove sits down on a wet cushion. "Goodbye, old thing," he says. "I hope you find wherever you're going." Pip waves his towel at it.

variants.text: Without the island's fresh magic to chase, the crawlers lose interest and clatter back toward their tear.
You chased the crawlers off, and now they are scattered over the temple roofs, clicking.

settled.narration: Notchbrow's edge nudges the landing and stops. It rests there at last, grass dripping, its old stone just across the rail. Clove hangs a sign on the gate: PLEASE KNOCK, EVEN IF YOU ARE AN ISLAND.

variants.text: The cushions squash, and not one board cracks.
Crunch. The landing rail bends flat. Clove sighs, then grins. "Rails can be mended. Islands can't be hurried."
Without the island's fresh magic to chase, the crawlers lose interest and clatter back toward their tear.
You chased the crawlers off, and now they are scattered over the temple roofs, clicking.

damaged.narration: The crawlers drive everyone back inside the hall. Outside, Notchbrow bumps the empty landing, hard. Boards crack, a lantern post topples, and the landing breaks in two. Then the island swings away into the rain. Everyone is safe and dry, but the landing is gone. "Closed for repairs," Clove says bravely, and hangs the sign upside down. The crawlers have the yard to themselves.

choices.label: Wait for the storm to ease

crawlers_home.narration: The squall begins to ease. By the tower, the tear in the air is shrinking. But crawlers still cling to the warm bells, clicking sadly. They are a very long way from home. Pip holds out his spoon to one. "They want to go home," he says. "Everything does." How will you get them through before the tear closes?

variants.text: After the fight they won, there are a lot of them.

check_hum.narration: You hum low and steady, like the bells. Clove hums along, a little off key.
check_hum.prompt: Hum the crawlers down from the bells and through the shrinking tear

onSuccess.narration: The crawlers sway to your tune, then trot through the tear one by one, back toward their faraway bones.

onFailure.narration: Your hum wobbles. The crawlers go, all but one. It tucks itself inside the weather bell and will not budge.

check_sweep.narration: Clove hands out brooms. The crawlers cling to the bells with all their legs.
check_sweep.prompt: Sweep the clinging crawlers down and through the tear

onSuccess.narration: Swish, swish. The crawlers skitter through the tear, offended but home.

onFailure.narration: Swish! One crawler dodges the broom and hides inside the weather bell. It will not come out.

tear_shut.narration: The tear folds shut like a sleepy eye. The rain stops. Through a gap in the clouds, the sun comes out over a hundred islands, and the wet roofs shine. Clove takes off his foggy glasses and cleans them on his apron, at last.

variants.text: From inside the bell comes a small click. Clove sighs. "Fine. You can be the temple's bell crawler. No chewing."

fig_thanks.narration: Fig pads up with something behind her back: a drawing of Notchbrow, with all of you standing in front of it, very small and very brave. "For you," she whispers, and runs away before anyone can say thank you. Pip looks at it for a long time.

farewell.narration: Clove opens his weather book to a fresh page and dips his pen. "I write one line about every storm," he says. "What should tonight's line be?"

choices.label: Even crawlers want to go home

clove_pulled.narration: Clove writes it slowly: Something is pulling the land. Then he underlines it twice. "Every keeper who reads this book will watch the sky a little harder now," he says.

clove_home.narration: Clove writes it, smiling: Even crawlers want to go home. "That's the truest line in this whole book," he says. Pip copies it onto the back of his paw.

ending.narration: Tumble lands on the shining landing, almost gracefully. "Griffin flight down to a mountain pass called the Cairnstep?" she offers. "Or back to Juniper's lookout. I'll try very hard to land." So here is your piece: the pull reaches everywhere. It drags islands across the sky, and crawlers all the way from the far-off coast. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Notchbrow rests beside the temple now, a neighbor that knocks.
Somewhere out in the clearing sky, Notchbrow drifts on, still pulled.
The landing is closed for repairs, but every keeper is safe, and Notchbrow has drifted on.
The weather bell was silent tonight, so the other islands will have a soggy morning.
Inside the bell, the bell crawler clicks goodbye.
Pip stays right beside you, just as he promised.
Tumble has waited all evening on the roof for you.
Tumble has flown in at last, her letters finally dry.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
